building.name: International Building Code with Utah amendments (Utah State Construction Code)
building.local_amendments_note: One Salt Lake City amendment is written into state law, Utah Code 15A-4-106: delayed-egress panic hardware in assembly areas of the International Airport. It does not touch toilet rooms. Salt Lake City Code Title 18 (administrative provisions) applies 'to a limited extent'; it could not be opened (American Legal's code library returned 403).
building.quote: (1) Subject to the other provisions of this part, the following construction codes are incorporated by reference, and together with the amendments specified in Chapter 3, Statewide Amendments Incorporated as Part of State Construction Code, and Chapter 4, Local Amendments Incorporated as Part of State Construction Code, are the construction standards to be applied to building construction, alteration, remodeling, and repair, and in the regulation of building construction, alteration, remodeling, and repair in the state: (a) the 2024 edition of the International Building Code, including Appendices C and J, issued by the International Code Council; [...] (d) the 2024 edition of the International Plumbing Code, issued by the International Code Council;
building.city_quote: Salt Lake City follows the building and fire codes adopted and amended by the State of Utah. To a limited extent, Salt Lake City building codes are also applicable and can be found in Title 18. [...] Salt Lake City Code sections pertaining to construction also apply to an extent limited by Utah Code, including Section 15A-1-204(8).
building.local_amendment_quote: 15A-4-106 Amendments to IBC applicable to Salt Lake City. The following amendment is adopted as an amendment to the IBC for Salt Lake City, in IBC, Section 1008.1.9.7, a new exception is added as follows: "Exception: In International Airport areas designated as Group "A" Occupancies where national security interests are present, the use of panic hardware with delayed egress is allowed when all provisions of Section 1008.1.9.7 are met and under item #4 1 second is changed to 2 seconds." Enacted by Chapter 14, 2011 General Session

fixtures.basis: Utah Code Title 15A, Chapter 4 was read in full (the Legislature's PDF of the chapter). Part 1 (building code) has entries for Park City, Salt Lake City and Sandy; the Salt Lake City entry, 15A-4-106, concerns delayed-egress panic hardware at the International Airport only. Part 3 (plumbing code) has an entry for South Jordan only. Utah Code 15A-1-204(8) bars a city from adopting a requirement more restrictive than the State Construction Code on a subject it addresses, and Salt Lake City's own page says it follows the codes 'adopted and amended by the State of Utah'. The state pack's counts stand.

permit.exempt_list_quote: **Most construction projects require a permit. Exceptions include painting, laying flooring or other cosmetic issues. Other exemptions include: playhouses, sheds, and similar uses under 200 square feet for residential uses and 120 for commercial uses; oil derricks; movable cases, counters and partitions not over five feet high; retaining walls which are not over four feet in height measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, unless supporting a surcharge or impounding flammable liquids; water tanks supported directly upon grade if the capacity does not exceed five thousand gallons and the ratio of height to diameter or width does not exceed two to one; painting, papering and similar finish work; temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery; window awnings supported by an exterior wall of Group R, Division 3, and Group M occupancies, when projecting not more than 54 inches. Please contact the Permits Office with questions. The permit staff can be reached at 801-535-6000
permit.note: The city's list names 'movable cases, counters and partitions not over five feet high' and 'painting, papering and similar finish work'. Toilet partitions (anchored to floor, wall or ceiling) are not named. The same page says alterations to a building's layout usually need a permit and 'A building permit is required for interior demolition of a structure.' The building code's own list (2024 IBC Section 105.2, which Utah's amendments in 15A-3-102 leave unchanged) reads slightly differently: item 13 is 'Nonfixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches (1753 mm) in height' and item 7 is 'Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work.' Neither names toilet partitions. Salt Lake City Code Title 18 (18.20, permits) could not be opened.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Salt Lake City job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Utah rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Salt Lake City offices, schools, clinics and distribution centers, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Utah's plumbing rules set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building, and Salt Lake City applies them unchanged. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Salt Lake City says most construction projects need a permit. Its list of exceptions covers painting, flooring and similar finish work, and movable partitions not over five feet high. It doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask Salt Lake City Building Services whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.install_rule: On a commercial property, Salt Lake City issues permits only to state-licensed contractors, and the contractor obtains the permit where one is needed. Utah requires a contractor license for alteration or remodel work valued at $7,000 or more, labor and materials included; between $3,000 and $7,000 the contractor files a one-time insurance statement with the state. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: On a job worth $7,000 or more, the contractor needs a Utah contractor license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Utah has no state wage law for public construction, so set wage rates apply only on federally funded projects. For a carpenter on building work in Salt Lake County the federal rate is $20.66 an hour plus $7.47 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.45% in Salt Lake City: 4.85% state, 1% local, 0.25% county, 1.25% in transit and transportation taxes, 0.1% for botanical, cultural and zoo organizations, a 0.5% correctional facility tax and a 0.5% capital city revitalization tax.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals and university buildings:** phenolic or stainless steel where restrooms are cleaned often, with full-height privacy options.
sources: - Codes Salt Lake City enforces: Salt Lake City Building Services, [Current Building Codes](https://www.slc.gov/buildingservices/current-building-codes/) ("Salt Lake City follows the building and fire codes adopted and amended by the State of Utah"), and [Utah Code 15A-2-103](https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title15A/Chapter2/C15A-2-S103_2026050620260701.html) (2024 International Building Code and 2024 International Plumbing Code, version effective July 1, 2026; the [version effective January 1, 2027](https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title15A/Chapter2/C15A-2-S103_2026050620270101.html) keeps both editions). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Local amendments, and toilet counts being the state's in Salt Lake City: [Utah Code Title 15A, Chapter 4, Local Amendments Incorporated as Part of State Construction Code](https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title15A/Chapter4/C15A-4_1800010118000101.pdf). Section 15A-4-106, the only Salt Lake City entry, covers exit hardware at the International Airport; Part 3 (plumbing code) has no Salt Lake City entry. Cities may not be stricter than the state code: [Utah Code 15A-1-204](https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title15A/Chapter1/C15A-1-S204_2025110620251206.html). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Permits and work exempt from a permit in Salt Lake City: Salt Lake City Building Services, [Building permit FAQs](https://www.slc.gov/buildingservices/building-permits/faqs/) ("When do I need a permit?"). The building code's own list, 2024 International Building Code Section 105.2, was read on a [secondary copy of the Utah Building Code 2024](https://up.codes/viewer/utah/ibc-2024/chapter/1/scope-and-administration); Utah's amendments to Chapter 1 leave it unchanged: [Utah Code 15A-3-102](https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title15A/Chapter3/C15A-3-S102_2026050620260701.html). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Contractors on commercial property in Salt Lake City: Salt Lake City Building Services, [Building permit FAQs](https://www.slc.gov/buildingservices/building-permits/faqs/) ("When do I need a contractor?", "Who is responsible for getting the permit?"). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax in Salt Lake City: Utah State Tax Commission, [Combined Sales and Use Tax Rates, in effect October 1, 2026](https://files.tax.utah.gov/tax/salestax/rate/26q4combined.pdf) and [in effect January 1, 2027](https://files.tax.utah.gov/tax/salestax/rate/27q1combined.pdf), location code 18-122; the 8.45% rate first appears on the [chart in effect July 1, 2025](https://files.tax.utah.gov/tax/salestax/rate/25q3combined.pdf). Rate charts: [Sales and Use Tax Rates](https://tax.utah.gov/sales/rates). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Salt Lake County carpenter rate on federally funded building work: [federal wage determination UT20260085, modification 1, May 18, 2026](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/UT20260085/1). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; ICC A117.1-2009 (Utah Code 15A-3-113); Utah State Construction Code: 2024 International Building Code and 2024 International Plumbing Code with Utah amendments (Utah Code 15A-2-103, version effective July 1, 2026; Title 15A, Chapter 3), enforced by Salt Lake City with one local amendment that does not concern restrooms (Utah Code 15A-4-106); Salt Lake City Code Title 18, Buildings and Construction; NFPA 286 for HDPE.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether a like-for-like replacement of anchored toilet partitions needs a Salt Lake City permit (Permits Office, 801-535-6000; plans examiner, 801-535-7155).
Salt Lake City Code Title 18 (American Legal code library) could not be opened: read chapter 18.20 (permits) and search the code for restroom sign rules once in a browser.
The city's FAQ gives 'five feet high' for movable partitions; the 2024 building code's list says 5 feet 9 inches. The page follows the city's wording.

Sales tax: the Tax Commission's charts are not meant for out-of-state sellers, who source by the buyer's ZIP+4. One area inside the city limits (MIDA Salt Lake City, code 18-301) is charted at 10.05%; check a delivery address with the Tax Commission's lookup.
Recheck the rate chart each quarter (tax.utah.gov/sales/rates); 8.45% is confirmed through the January 1, 2027 chart.

The federal carpenter rate used is the general carpenter line of UT20260085 ($20.66 + $7.47, a 2014 survey rate). The same determination has a union rate of $31.66 + $13.97 for drywall hanging and metal stud installation only.
The date the 2024 codes took effect in Utah (July 1, 2026) comes from the heading of the statute version; the previous version of 15A-2-103 was not opened.
The meta description doesn't mention climate: Salt Lake City is dry (15.5 inches of precipitation a year), so the material section carries that.
